tags: @guarantee ok.constructs-ok `ok(value)` constructs an `Ok` variant of `Result`.
@guarantee ok.is-ok-true `ok({ myData: "test" }).isOk()` is `true` and `.isErr()` is `false`.
@guarantee ok.constructs-err `err(error)` constructs an `Err` variant of `Result`.
@guarantee ok.is-err-true `err("Oh noooo").isOk()` is `false` and `.isErr()` is `true`.
@guarantee ok.true-for-ok `isOk` returns `true` when the result is an `Ok` variant.
@guarantee ok.false-for-ok `isErr` returns `false` when the result is an `Ok` variant.
@guarantee ok.false-for-err `isOk` returns `false` when the result is an `Err` variant.
@guarantee ok.true-for-err `isErr` returns `true` when the result is an `Err` variant.
@guarantee ok.applies-callback `map` applies the callback to the contained `Ok` value and returns a `Result` holding the callback's return value as `Ok`.
@guarantee ok.leaves-err `map` leaves an `Err` value untouched and does not apply the callback.
@guarantee ok.leaves-ok `mapErr` leaves an `Ok` value untouched.
@guarantee ok.applies-callback `mapErr` applies the callback to the contained `Err` value and returns a `Result` holding the callback's return value as `Err`.
@guarantee ok.unwraps-value `unwrapOr` returns the `Ok` value, not the default.
@guarantee ok.returns-default `unwrapOr` returns the given default when the result is an `Err`, so `err("Oh noooo").map(multiply).unwrapOr(10)` gives 10.
@guarantee ok.chains-results `andThen` calls the callback with the `Ok` value and returns the `Result` the callback returns.

@guarantee ok.chain-examples With `sq` returning `ok(n ** 2)`, `ok(2).andThen(sq).andThen(sq)` is `Ok(16)`, `ok(2).andThen(sq).andThen(err)` is `Err(4)` and `ok(2).andThen(err).andThen(sq)` is `Err(2)`.
@guarantee ok.flattens-nested `ok(ok(1234)).andThen` with a callback returning its argument gives `Ok(1234)`.
@guarantee ok.keeps-err With `sq` returning `ok(n ** 2)`, `err(3).andThen(sq).andThen(sq)` is `Err(3)`.
@guarantee ok.recovers `orElse` takes the `Err` value and maps it to the `Result` returned by the callback, so a callback returning `ok("User does not exist")` recovers the error into an `Ok`.
@guarantee ok.runs-ok-callback `match` executes the first function (the `Ok` callback) with the value and returns its return value, without requiring it to return a `Result`.
@guarantee ok.runs-err-callback `match` executes the second function (the `Err` callback) with the error and returns its return value, without requiring it to return a `Result`.
@guarantee ok.passes-through `andTee` lets the original `Ok` result pass through regardless of the result of the passed-in function.
@guarantee ok.passes-through `orTee` lets the original `Err` result pass through regardless of the result of the passed-in function.
@guarantee ok.passes-error-along When the function passed to `andThrough` returns an error, that error is passed along.
